newsitem.title: PANAMA: Ecuador's deposed president seeks asylum in Panama.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's deposed president seeks asylum in Panama.

text.p: Ecuador's deposed President Abdala Bucaram said on Thursday he had asked for political asylum in Panama, where he fled following his ouster two months ago.
"I asked the Panamanian government for asylum 20 days ago for seven people -- my wife, children and brother Santiago," Bucaram told a news conference.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Erich Rodriguez said the Panamanian government was reviewing Bucaram's request.
Bucaram was deposed by the Ecuadorean Congress on Feb. 6 for "mental incompetence" after only six months in power.

Ecuador's Supreme Court on Wednesday issued an order for his arrest and extradition on the grounds that he misused government funds. But Bucaram sounded confident, noting there was no extradition treaty betwen Ecuador and Panama.
"I don't think the extradition will occur because they have to go through a legal process," he said.

Bucaram, whose presidency ended in a wave of popular protests and strikes, vowed to return "clandestinely" to Ecuador. He gave no details. In the meantime, he said he hoped Panama would allow him to continue his political activities.

The colourful populist leader, who continues to call himself president and has promised to run again in elections next year, already lived in Panama from 1985-90 after fleeing charges of corruption as mayor of his home city Guayaquil.
"I like living in Panama City," said Bucaram, who took up residence in Panama City's posh Punta Paitilla district. But he added: "I would like to be president one more time."
